findings.evidence: “Context. Engine and version, workload, scale, tenancy, retention, and whether the schema is new or already live” and “Integrity. Keys, nullability, uniqueness, FK delete behavior, checks, tenant ownership, soft-delete policy and time types” repeat standard schema-design inventories. By H2 line weight, Defaults and References are chiefly activation/routing, Workflow mixes familiar modeling guidance with useful decisions, and Gotchas supplies most of the expert delta.
findings.fix: Condense the routine context, requirements and integrity inventories into one prerequisite instruction. Preserve explicit defaults, the atomic-write-boundary question, engine-specific gotchas and live-migration sequences; prioritize non-obvious decisions over familiar checklist content.

findings.evidence: The NOT NULL procedure describes ADD CHECK NOT VALID as a “brief lock” followed by VALIDATE CONSTRAINT so “reads and writes continue.” However, SKILL.md directs migration files to start from assets/templates/migration-template.sql, whose PostgreSQL example encloses DDL in BEGIN/COMMIT. Following that template for this sequence retains the ADD CHECK ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock throughout validation, blocking traffic during the scan.
findings.fix: Require ADD CHECK NOT VALID, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, and SET NOT NULL to run in separately committed migrations or transactions. Explicitly prohibit wrapping the entire sequence in the template's single transaction, and apply a bounded lock timeout to each phase.

findings.evidence: “Use NUMERIC/DECIMAL with a fixed scale or integer minor units” is presented without an engine restriction, although SQLite is explicitly supported. In SQLite, DECIMAL(p,s) has NUMERIC affinity, does not enforce the declared precision or scale, and can store fractional amounts as binary floating-point REAL values, defeating the stated money invariant.
findings.fix: Make the money rule engine-specific: use fixed-scale NUMERIC/DECIMAL on PostgreSQL and MySQL; default to INTEGER minor units with a documented currency scale and range checks on SQLite. Do not describe SQLite DECIMAL declarations as enforcing exact fixed-scale storage.

findings.evidence: “Delete or merge any index that duplicates a leading prefix of another” treats a matching column prefix as sufficient proof of redundancy. For example, UNIQUE (organization_id, slug) is not replaced by a non-unique index on (organization_id, slug, created_at); following the cleanup rule can remove an integrity guarantee. Different partial-index predicates likewise invalidate the shortcut.
findings.fix: Treat a matching leading prefix only as a candidate for review. Before removal, compare constraint ownership, uniqueness semantics, predicates, expressions, operator classes, collation and ordering, then verify workload plans. Explicitly preserve constraint-backed indexes unless an equivalent constraint remains enforced.
